title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: Opening an Account and Its First Deposit
content:
This page governs how a Savings & Money Market Accounts product comes into being: the state a new account starts in, the tests applied on the opening date, how the first deposit brings the account to life, what happens to an account that is never funded, and how the end of a promotional period is fixed for the tiers that offer one.

## Rule

**Starting position.** A newly opened account sits in applied status, with a balance of zero and no automatic transfer set up.

**Age on the opening date.** The customer's age in completed years on the opening date, worked out from the date of birth held on the customer profile, has to reach the minimum opening age of the chosen tier. What the customer says about their age does not replace the profile.

**Checking relationship.** Where the chosen tier names one or more Personal Checking tiers as a requirement, the customer must, on the opening date, already have an active checking account of one of those tiers, as the bank's checking records show for that customer. A tier that names none imposes no such test.

**First deposit.** Activation happens on the business day the first deposit posts, and only where that deposit reaches the tier's smallest first deposit. A first deposit below that figure is sent back and leaves the account in applied status.

**Unfunded accounts.** An account that remains in applied status is closed as unfunded when **30** calendar days have gone by since it was opened. Days are counted from the day following the opening date, which is day 1; the closure falls due once the current date is the opening date moved forward by 30 days, or any later date.

**Promotion end date.** On a tier that pays a promotional rate, the date the promotion ends is fixed when the account opens: the opening date carried forward by the tier's promotional length in calendar months. If the resulting month has no such day, the last day of that month is used.

The age, checking, first-deposit and promotion figures used are those of the tier being opened.

## Opening-day checklist

| Test | Evidence | Satisfied when |
|---|---|---|
| Age | date of birth on the customer profile | completed years on the opening date reach the tier minimum |
| Checking relationship (only tiers that name one) | the customer's checking accounts on file | one active account of a named tier exists on the opening date |
| Activation | the first posted deposit | it is at least the tier's smallest first deposit |

## Boundary cases for the unfunded closure (hypothetical dates)

- Opened on 2 March and still unfunded: day 1 is 3 March and day 30 is 1 April. On 1 April the closure is due; on 31 March it is not yet due.
- Opened on 15 January: 30 days on is 14 February. The account is closed as unfunded from 14 February onward if no qualifying deposit has posted; on 13 February it stays in applied status.

## Promotion end date examples (hypothetical)

- Opened 10 May on a tier with a six-month promotion: the promotion ends 10 November.
- Opened 31 August on a tier with a six-month promotion: February has no 31st, so the promotion ends on the last day of that February.
